key_insight: A hierarchical multilevel Monte Carlo critic removes the neural bias-cost bottleneck, enabling order-optimal primal-dual actor-critic learning for average-reward CMDPs with neural critics.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical path to safe reinforcement learning in long-horizon control systems where both reward maximization and constraint satisfaction must be guaranteed.
method: Use an MLMC neural critic to debias estimates across both trajectory sampling and critic optimization.
Embed the critic inside a primal-dual natural actor-critic framework for average-reward CMDPs.
Leverage the estimator’s logarithmic expected sample cost to achieve tilde{O}(T^{-1/2}) optimality gap and constraint violation.
evidence_signal: The abstract claims the first order-optimal convergence guarantees for infinite-horizon average-reward CMDPs with general policy parameterization and neural critics, without requiring knowledge of mixing time.
watch_item: The approach relies on NTK-style analysis and a hierarchical MLMC critic, so practical performance may depend on approximation quality, optimization stability, and careful implementation of multi-level sampling.
paper_title: Hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo for Order-Optimal Neural Actor-Critic in Average-Reward CMDPs
